case.title: Reliable Fire Equipment Co. v. Arredondo
case.holding: Covenants not to compete are enforceable if reasonable, judged by the totality of the circumstances.
case.reasoning: Employer must show a legitimate business interest; factors include customer permanence, confidential information, and reasonable time/place restrictions.
case.conclusion: Remanded to trial court to apply proper standard.
case.dicta: Court rejected rigid tests in favor of a flexible totality-of-the-circumstances analysis.

actionable_conduct: Forming a competitor company while having a non-compete signed
Soliciting customers in violation of non-solicitation agreement

Consideration.fact-point: Each defendant signed a noncompetition agreement in exchange for employment.

circumstances.Tenure: Arredondo was employed from 1980 until resignation in 2004; Garcia hired in 1998, terminated in 2004.

Position / Customer Relations.fact-point: Defendants had customer contact and solicited sales. Court noted 'near-permanence of customer relationships' as factor.
Position / Customer Relations.law-point: This is a Protectable Legitimate Business Interest

Blue Pencil.fact-point: Court refused blue-pencil, so the restrictive clause was preserved without a change.
